blocks.text: Money without Masters. Trust without People.
LEVEL 01: NOOB
Imagine a Google Sheet that tracks who owns what money. But:

items: ✅ No single spreadsheet owner; network participants follow shared rules.
✅ Many participants keep copies or verify the shared record.
✅ Network rules determine which proposed updates are accepted (consensus).
🔒 Confirmed records can be difficult to alter, though network reorganisations and protocol changes are possible.

blocks.text: This is Blockchain. Bitcoin is just the first app running on this system.

A public ledger can make transfers visible and difficult to alter, but it does not guarantee that a token has useful rights, stable value, safe software, or an honest operator. Separate the technology claim from the investment claim.
blocks.title: 🧾 Ledger Is Not the Whole Story

blocks.text: LEVEL 02: MECHANIC

Common comparison: Some people view Bitcoin as a scarce digital asset; its price and purchasing power can still fall.
Supply: Bitcoin’s current protocol rules cap issuance near 21 million coins. The network enforces those rules, but scarcity does not guarantee price appreciation or protection from inflation.
blocks.title: 🥇 Bitcoin (BTC) = Digital Gold

blocks.text:
Purpose: Fuel for the Global Computer.
Transactions: On Ethereum mainnet, ETH is generally used to pay transaction fees (gas). Smart contracts support apps and financial services, each with its own technical and market risks.
blocks.title: 🛢️ Ethereum (ETH) = Digital Oil

blocks.text: Bitcoin and Ethereum have different design goals, security assumptions, and ecosystems. A simple analogy can help you remember a distinction, but it cannot replace understanding how a network validates transactions and what its token is used for.
blocks.title: 🧩 Different Networks, Different Roles

blocks.text: LEVEL 03: PRO
Before buying any "Altcoin", check these two numbers:
Market Cap
Current Price x Circulating Supply
"What it's worth today"
FDV
Current Price x TOTAL Supply
"What it's worth if all tokens unlock"

⚠️ A large gap between market capitalisation and fully diluted valuation can signal substantial potential future supply. Check the unlock schedule, who holds those tokens, and whether demand could absorb them; the ratio alone does not predict price.

Check circulating supply, maximum or planned supply, unlock schedules, concentration among large holders, and the rights attached to a token. Fully diluted valuation can highlight future supply, but it does not predict whether demand will exist.
blocks.title: 🔍 Supply Questions

blocks.text:
"Not your Keys, Not your Coins."
When a platform holds assets for you, you depend on its custody, security, solvency, and legal terms. If it fails, access or recovery may be delayed and is not assured. Self-custody removes that intermediary but makes you responsible for securing the keys.
Trade-off: A hardware wallet can keep signing keys offline, but it does not remove software, user, recovery, or market risks. Understand the recovery process before moving assets.
blocks.title: ☠️ GOD MODE: Self-Custody

blocks.text: With self-custody, losing the recovery phrase can mean losing access permanently; sharing it can let someone take the assets. With a platform, you depend on its security, controls, and solvency. Virtual digital assets have specific tax and reporting rules; check current Income Tax Department guidance before transacting.
blocks.title: 🔐 Custody Check

sources.label: check current Income Tax Department guidance
